Design 01 · Modular Harness Exosuit

Independent modules,
an open harness.

An open shoulder harness and a separate waist belt carry two protected rear working modules. Passive transfer straps continue to independently adjustable thigh cuffs, keeping the torso centre open.

Design principle

Keep each module, attachment, and fit adjustment identifiable.

Workwear reference

Logistics equipment harnesses inform the chest-device mount, accessible waist belt and independently adjustable lower interfaces.

              DESIGN REFERENCE

              Modular Harness Exosuit

              Front and rear three-quarter design views supplied by the designer.

              ABOUT

              Three ways to wear an exosuit.

              Wearable Exosuit Visual Design is a November 2026 design study of wearable concepts around a concealed textile-actuation system for lifting and bending assistance.

              Design objectives

              • Organize the shoulder, back, waist and thigh interfaces.
              • Make fitting controls and battery access easy to identify.
              • Explore different levels of integration with workwear.

              From exploration to selection

              Sixteen early concepts explored eight structural arrangements and eight occupational workwear directions. Three retained structures develop an open harness, a vest with thigh interfaces, and a top paired with support shorts.

              Modular Harness Exosuit
              Individually bounded modules attach to an open, adjustable harness.
              Vest-Mounted Exosuit
              A contoured external module mounts on a shared vest carrier.
              Garment-Integrated Exosuit
              The working region sits within the layered back garment panel.

              Reference approach

              The reference analysis brings together textile assistance harnesses, industrial back-support packaging, and garment-integrated systems. Workwear studies inform device placement, garment openings, closures and the organization of body-contact regions.

              About the interactive models

              Each design offers a Human + Exosuit view and a separate Exosuit Only view. The mannequin views show garment placement and body relationships; the standalone views allow inspection of the equipment with independent framing and component hotspots. Models, concept illustrations and reference dimensions support visual design review.

              Active length, contraction travel, cooling and fit remain under development. Source references and garment analogies inform the design without establishing engineering performance.
